courses.title: Common Core Training
courses.short_description: The mandatory 16-hour foundation for every VTIARA role: values, patient communication, hygiene, consent, privacy and emergencies.
courses.overview: Every new hire completes the Common Core first, over 2.5 days (6 + 5.5 + 4.5 hours), before any role training. It gives everyone the same safe, patient-first foundation through classroom sessions, demonstrations, role-play and a short quiz. Its 16 hours are counted inside each role's total hours.
courses.audience: All new hires: therapists, nurses, dermatologists, housekeeping, telecallers, front desk and managers.
outcomes: Greet and treat patients with the VTIARA standard of courtesy and privacy
Explain, in simple words, what skin and hair are and why hygiene matters
Clean hands correctly at the right moments and use gloves and masks properly
Separate waste into the right colour bin
Handle consent, photos and patient information without breaking privacy
Act correctly in a fainting, allergic reaction or fire emergency
requirements_text: 100% attendance
80% or higher on the 20-question knowledge test (16 of 20)
Hand hygiene practical passed

modules.title: C1 Welcome, VTIARA values, grooming and behaviour

lessons.title: The VTIARA story and our values
lessons.description: Each person can state the VTIARA values and shows correct grooming and conduct.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- VTIARA story, branch map, who does what in a branch
- Values: safety first, honesty, respect, same standard in every branch

lessons.title: Grooming, attendance and conduct
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Dress code, ID badge, nails, hair, light perfume; punctuality, attendance and leave rules
- Phone use on the floor; no gossip about patients; no photos without consent

lessons.title: Anti-harassment (POSH) and good service
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Anti-harassment policy (POSH) and whom to approach
- Practice: discuss good and bad service scenes and write 3 rules each

lessons.title: Greeting and listening
lessons.description: Each person greets, listens and responds to a patient in simple, respectful words.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Greeting standard: smile, name, offer help within 10 seconds
- Active listening; plain words instead of medical jargon; never promise results

lessons.title: Upset patients, phone and WhatsApp
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Upset patients: Listen, Apologise, Solve, Thank; when to call the nurse, doctor or manager
- Tone on phone and WhatsApp
- Practice: pair role-play of 4 scenarios (long wait, price complaint, anxious patient, wrong appointment)

modules.title: C3 Skin and hair basics in plain language

lessons.title: Skin basics
lessons.description: Each person can explain skin and hair basics and knows when to call the doctor.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Skin layers (epidermis, dermis, hypodermis), skin functions
- Skin types: oily, dry, combination, sensitive; why sun protection matters

lessons.title: Hair basics
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Hair structure; growth cycle (growing, transition, resting phases)
- Losing about 50-100 hairs a day is normal

lessons.title: Common problems and our limits
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Names and meaning of common problems: acne, pigmentation, dandruff, hair fall
- Staff never diagnose; they say 'the doctor will examine you'
- Practice: label skin and hair diagrams; myth-or-fact quiz

modules.title: C4 Hygiene, infection control and waste

lessons.title: How infection spreads and standard precautions
lessons.description: Each person cleans hands correctly, uses PPE, handles sharps safely and sorts waste.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- How infection spreads; standard precautions for every patient

lessons.title: Hand hygiene: the 5 moments
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Before touching a patient; before a clean or aseptic task; after body-fluid exposure risk; after touching a patient; after touching patient surroundings
- Hand rub 20-30 seconds until dry; wash with soap and water 40-60 seconds when hands are visibly dirty

lessons.title: PPE and cleaning levels
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Gloves, masks, aprons, eye protection: when and how to put on and remove; gloves come off first
- Clean, disinfect, sterilise: what each means

lessons.title: Sharps, needle-stick and waste colour bins
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Never recap or bend needles; use the sharps container; needle-stick response
- Biomedical waste colour bins and spill basics
- Practice: hand hygiene practical, PPE sequence, waste-sorting game

lessons.title: Consent
lessons.description: Each person knows what consent is, handles photos and records correctly and keeps patient information private.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Consent must be informed, written for procedures, and can be withdrawn
- Photos need separate consent; minors need a guardian

lessons.title: Privacy and patient data
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Share patient information only with the treating team; never on personal phones or WhatsApp groups
- Collect only needed data and keep it safe under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
- Practice: 3 case studies (relative asks for a report, photo for social media, lost file)

modules.title: C6 Safety, fire and emergency awareness

lessons.title: Exits, alarms and first actions
lessons.description: Each person knows exits, alarms, extinguishers and the first actions in a fainting, allergic reaction or fire.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Exits, assembly point, alarm, extinguisher locations
- Rule for any emergency: call for help first, then act within your training
- Fainting, allergic reaction signs, and fire (RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Evacuate or Extinguish)
- Practice: branch walk-through; mock fainting drill

lessons.title: Knowledge test and practical sign-off
lessons.description: 20-question knowledge test (30 minutes, pass mark 80%) and trainer-observed hand hygiene practical.
lessons.transcript:
Knowledge test: 20 questions, 30 minutes, 16 of 20 correct to pass. Below 80%: revise with the trainer and retake after 3 days.
Hand hygiene practical: trainer checklist.
Records: attendance sheet, test score, handout acknowledgement, signed code of conduct.

questions.q: How long should you rub alcohol-based hand rub over all hand surfaces?
o: Only until it stops feeling wet
questions.e: Alcohol-based rub needs 20–30 seconds of contact and should be rubbed until your hands are dry.

questions.q: Your hands are visibly soiled. What should you use?
questions.e: Visibly soiled hands must be washed with soap and water; rub is not enough.

questions.q: Which is one of the five moments for hand hygiene?
o: Only at the start of your shift
questions.e: The five moments include before touching a patient, before a clean/aseptic task, after body-fluid exposure, after touching a patient and after touching patient surroundings.

questions.q: After removing gloves you should:
o: Do nothing, gloves kept hands clean
questions.e: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Clean your hands after removing them.

questions.q: Standard precautions apply to:
o: Only patients who ask for them
questions.e: Standard precautions treat every patient's blood and body fluids as potentially infectious.

questions.q: A reusable instrument has just been used on a patient. What do you do?
o: Wipe it and use it on the next patient
Treat it as contaminated and send it for decontamination per protocol
Rinse under the tap and keep it on the tray
Leave it in the treatment room
questions.e: Used instruments are contaminated until they go through the clinic's decontamination and sterilisation process.

questions.q: Where do used needles and other sharps go?
questions.e: Sharps go into a puncture-proof, leak-proof sharps container (white translucent under the Bio-Medical Waste Rules).

questions.q: You have just used a needle. What must you never do?
o: Dispose of it immediately in the sharps container
Recap or bend it by hand
Keep the container below fill line
questions.e: Never recap or bend needles; this is a leading cause of needle-stick injuries.

questions.q: Blood-soiled cotton and dressings are segregated into:
questions.e: Soiled waste such as blood-stained cotton and dressings goes into the yellow category bag.

questions.q: Before any procedure, patient consent must be:
o: Assumed if the patient booked an appointment
Informed, voluntary and documented as per clinic policy
Taken verbally from a relative only
questions.e: Valid consent is informed, voluntary and recorded before the procedure begins.

questions.q: A patient hesitates and asks you to stop during a procedure. You:
o: Finish quickly as it is almost done
Stop and inform the doctor or supervisor
Ignore it if they are quiet
questions.e: Consent can be withdrawn at any time. Stop safely and escalate.

questions.q: You need a photo of a patient's treatment area for the record. You:
o: Use your personal phone for convenience
Take it only with the patient's consent on an approved clinic device
Ask a colleague to take it on theirs
Skip consent if the face is not visible
questions.e: Photos need explicit consent and must be taken and stored only on approved clinic systems.

questions.q: A friend asks whether a well-known person visited the clinic. You:
o: Say nothing is confirmed or shared about any patient
questions.e: Never confirm or hint at who is or is not a patient.

questions.q: Patient details may be discussed:
o: Only with those who need to know, in a private place
questions.e: Share on a need-to-know basis and in private settings only.

questions.q: A colleague asks to use your system login 'just this once'. You:
o: Refuse; every user must use their own login
Share it and change it later
Write it on a sticky note for them
questions.e: Logins are personal. Sharing breaks audit trails and patient privacy.

questions.q: You step away from a computer showing a patient record. You should:
o: Ask the patient to watch it
questions.e: Lock the screen every time you leave a device.

questions.q: A patient asks which tablet to take for hair fall. You:
o: Suggest one you have heard works
Politely explain you cannot advise and connect them with the doctor
questions.e: Only qualified clinicians diagnose or prescribe. Refer clinical questions to the doctor.

questions.q: An upset patient complains about waiting. Your best first step is to:
o: Argue the wait was not long
Listen calmly, acknowledge the concern and escalate if unresolved
questions.e: Listening and acknowledging calms the situation; escalate to your supervisor when needed.

questions.q: A patient feels faint and slumps in the waiting area. You first:
o: Stay with the patient and alert the clinical team immediately
Wait to see if it passes
questions.e: Stay with the patient, call for help and follow the emergency protocol. Do not give medication.

questions.q: You discover a fire. What is the correct action?
o: Raise the alarm, alert others and follow the evacuation plan
questions.e: Raise the alarm, help others to safety and follow the evacuation plan.

items.label: Applies adequate product and covers all hand surfaces
Palm-to-palm, backs of hands and between fingers
Correct duration (20–30 s rub or 40–60 s wash)
Dries hands properly / rub left to dry

courses.title: Skin Therapist Training
courses.short_description: An 8-week, 280-hour programme that turns a trainee into a safe, consistent skin and hair therapist. Nobody works on a patient until the Level 1 exams are passed.
courses.overview: Over 8 weeks (16 hours of Common Core plus 264 therapist hours: about 100 classroom and online, 90 hands-on lab and 90 supervised floor work) you learn skin and hair science, consultation support, facials and skin treatments, hair and scalp treatments, device and laser safety, and products and aftercare. Advanced devices need Level 2, and therapists never diagnose, prescribe or change the doctor's settings.
courses.audience: New therapists (skin, hair, facial), and existing therapists for upskilling.
eligibility: 12th pass plus beauty or skin diploma, or a fresher passing the aptitude test
outcomes: Analyse skin and scalp, name common conditions and know exactly when to call the doctor
Complete an intake, find contraindications, set honest expectations and document correctly
Perform approved facial and skin treatments safely and consistently
Perform scalp analysis and approved scalp treatments and assist doctor-led hair procedures
Understand device and laser safety and prepare and assist (independent operation needs Level 2)
Give honest product advice and the right aftercare
requirements_text: 100% attendance (missed days made up)
80% or higher on both knowledge tests
All practical stations passed with every critical item
Patient-safety check passed (100%)
Logbook minimums completed
Yearly practical and test; case review every quarter

lessons.title: Skin structure, types and the Fitzpatrick scale
lessons.description: The therapist can analyse skin and scalp, name common conditions and knows exactly when to call the doctor.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Skin layers and functions, the skin barrier, skin types
- Fitzpatrick scale (types I-VI) and how each type reacts to sun and procedures

lessons.title: Common skin conditions
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Acne and its grades, pigmentation (melasma, post-inflammatory), rosacea, eczema and dermatitis, ageing
- Recognise infections (fungal, bacterial, viral) and refer them
- Moles and spots that change (asymmetry, border, colour, diameter, evolving): always refer

lessons.title: Hair and scalp science
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Hair cycle (anagen, catagen, telogen); patterns of hair loss (androgenetic, stress-related shedding, patchy loss, traction)
- Scalp conditions such as dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis

lessons.title: Lifestyle, and why diagnosis is the doctor's job
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Nutrition, sleep, stress and hair; why diagnosis is the doctor's job
- Practice: skin type and Fitzpatrick identification on models; slide quiz; scalp photos

lessons.title: Intake and contraindication checks
lessons.description: The therapist completes an intake, finds contraindications, sets honest expectations and documents correctly.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Greeting, privacy, intake questions, medicines and allergies, pregnancy, skin and hair history
- Contraindication check; stop and call the doctor if in doubt

lessons.title: Expectations, consent and photos
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Results take weeks to months; never guarantee
- Consent forms; standard photo method (same light, angle, distance; no filters)

lessons.title: Handing the case to the doctor
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Handing the case to the doctor with a clear written note
- Practice: 6 mock consultations scored by the trainer

lessons.title: Set-up and hygiene
lessons.description: The therapist performs approved facial and skin treatments safely and consistently.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Room set-up, tool hygiene, patient positioning, hand hygiene
- Patch tests; product handling and shelf life

lessons.title: Facial steps
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Cleansing, gentle exfoliation, steam and its cautions, masks, LED light, hydration and hydrafacial-type treatments
- Extractions only of non-inflamed blackheads and whiteheads

lessons.title: Assisting peels and microneedling
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Assist superficial peels and microneedling when ordered by the doctor: preparing the skin, single-use sterile cartridges, timing, neutralising and soothing per the product protocol, immediate after-care

lessons.title: Standard facial and practice
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Standard facial time plan: 60 minutes
- Practice: 40 supervised facials in lab and floor

lessons.title: Scalp analysis
lessons.description: The therapist performs scalp analysis and approved scalp treatments and assists doctor-led hair procedures.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Scalp analysis with a trichoscope: capture and record, never diagnose

lessons.title: Scalp treatments
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Scalp cleansing and exfoliation, scalp massage, low-level light therapy

lessons.title: Assisting mesotherapy and PRP
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Assist mesotherapy and PRP when ordered: room and tray set-up, patient comfort, labelling; blood draw and preparation by the nurse or doctor
- Realistic timelines for hair regrowth; home-care routines
- Practice: 20 scalp analyses, 15 hair treatments with logbook entries

lessons.title: Light and skin
lessons.description: The therapist understands device safety and can prepare and assist; independent operation needs Level 2.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Simple light physics: wavelength, targets in skin, why skin type matters

lessons.title: Laser safety
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Laser safety officer role, door signs, correct protective eyewear for the device's wavelength for everyone in the room, cooling, emergency stop
- Settings are chosen by the doctor for each patient; therapists never change them

lessons.title: Daily checks and reactions
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Daily checks, consumables, cleaning, logs; test patch routine
- Burn and reaction first aid, then call the doctor
- Practice: device handling on practice models and approved training tools only; no patient use until Level 2

lessons.title: Common actives and sunscreen
lessons.description: The therapist gives honest product advice and the right aftercare.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- What common actives do: retinoids, AHA and BHA, vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid
- Sunscreen SPF 30 or higher, broad spectrum, reapplied every 2-3 hours outdoors

lessons.title: Aftercare and reactions
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Aftercare sheet for each treatment; recognising reactions; honest, no-pressure product advice

lessons.title: Supervised practice, logbook and exams
lessons.description: 40 hours of supervised floor practice and 16 hours of revision and exams.
lessons.transcript:
Assessment: knowledge test 1 (skin, hair, consultation) 40 MCQ in 60 minutes; knowledge test 2 (devices, safety, products) 30 MCQ in 45 minutes; both pass at 80%. Practical exam: facial, scalp analysis and a mock consultation, observed live; every critical item must be passed. Patient-safety check: contraindication scenario, reaction scenario and PPE, 100%.
Logbook minimums before Level 1: supervised facials 40; scalp analyses 20; hair or scalp treatments 15; consultations documented 30; device assists (no independent use) 20.

questions.q: A client shows a changing mole during a facial. You should:
o: Pause and refer the client to the doctor
questions.e: Anything outside therapist scope, including suspicious lesions, is referred to the doctor.

questions.q: Before a laser treatment starts, everyone in the room must:
questions.e: Correct protective eyewear is mandatory for all persons in the laser room.

questions.q: When should a procedure be recorded?
o: At the end of the week
Promptly and accurately after the procedure
questions.e: Timely, accurate records protect the patient and the clinic.

questions.q: The outermost layer of the skin is the:
questions.e: The epidermis is the outermost layer and forms the skin barrier.

checklist.title: Skin Therapist practical stations and logbook
checklist.description: Supervised practical stations and logbook review.

items.label: Logbook completed and signed by trainer

courses.title: Staff Nurse Training
courses.short_description: A 94-hour programme that makes a registered nurse safe and consistent in a VTIARA dermatology and hair clinic: sterility, medicines, emergencies and documentation.
courses.overview: Nurses are the clinic's safety backbone. Over about 2.5 weeks (16 hours of Common Core plus 78 nursing hours) you learn sterilisation and instrument processing, documentation and consent, medication handling, assisting clinic procedures, emergencies including BLS, and patient counselling. You never diagnose, prescribe, or perform a procedure that has not been ordered by the dermatologist.
courses.audience: Newly hired staff nurses, and existing nurses for refresher.
eligibility: Valid State Nursing Council registration (verified and copied to file)
outcomes: Process instruments so every item used on a patient is clean and sterile
Prepare patients and rooms, check consent and contraindication forms, and document correctly
Store, check and handle medicines safely, including the emergency tray
Prepare for and assist dermatologist-ordered procedures
Recognise and manage reactions and emergencies until the doctor arrives
Give aftercare instructions from approved sheets and confirm understanding
requirements_text: 100% attendance
80% or higher on the knowledge test
Both practical exams passed with all critical items
Emergency drill passed (100% of critical steps)
Logbook minimums completed
Yearly BLS renewal and re-certification

lessons.title: Item risk levels
lessons.description: The nurse processes instruments so that every item used on a patient is clean and sterile.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Critical (enter skin or blood), semi-critical, non-critical; what each needs

lessons.title: From dirty to sterile
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Point-of-use wipe, soak, manual or ultrasonic cleaning, rinse, dry, inspect, pack with indicator, sterilise, store

lessons.title: Steam sterilisation and load logs
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Cycle settings come from the autoclave and instrument manufacturers; chemical indicators in every pack; biological indicator tests as per policy
- Load logs, pack dates, shelf life, storage, recall of failed loads; single-use items are never reprocessed
- Practice: process a tray from dirty to sterile; read and sign a load log

lessons.title: The patient chart
lessons.description: The nurse keeps complete, accurate and private clinical records.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Patient chart, vitals, history, allergies, medication orders, procedure notes, aftercare given

lessons.title: Consent, photos and incident forms
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Written consent for procedures; separate photo consent; minors and guardians
- Incident and near-miss forms; privacy of records and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
- Practice: complete 5 mock charts; spot errors in 3 sample forms

lessons.title: Medication safety
lessons.description: The nurse stores, checks and gives medicines safely and records every step.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, right time, right documentation; check expiry and look-alike names

lessons.title: Storage and cold chain
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Room temperature items; refrigerator items at 2-8 degrees C with a twice-daily temperature log; report cold chain breaks

lessons.title: Topical anaesthetics and the emergency tray
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Topical anaesthetic creams only as ordered, on the specified area, for the time on the product label, then remove
- Emergency tray contents set by the Medical Advisor; weekly check with signed list
- Practice: read 10 orders and catch the errors; tray check

lessons.title: Room set-up and patient preparation
lessons.description: The nurse prepares patients and rooms and assists dermatologist-ordered procedures safely.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Room and tray set-up, patient identification, positioning and skin preparation

lessons.title: Assisting procedures
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Assisting peels, microneedling, PRP, mesotherapy and injectables as ordered by the dermatologist
- PRP blood draw and preparation per the device protocol; labelling of tubes

lessons.title: Dressings, monitoring and sharps
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Dressings and wound care; post-procedure monitoring; sharps handling
- Practice: set up and assist 10 mock procedures on models; observe 10 real procedures

lessons.title: Vital signs and when to call the doctor
lessons.description: The nurse recognises and manages reactions and emergencies until the doctor arrives.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Vital signs and when to call the doctor

lessons.title: Basic life support
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Adults: call for help, compressions at 100-120 a minute, depth 5-6 cm, 30 compressions to 2 breaths, AED as soon as available

lessons.title: Anaphylaxis and other emergencies
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Anaphylaxis, fainting, low blood sugar, seizure, burns (cool under running water for 20 minutes), signs of local anaesthetic toxicity
- Medicines in an emergency only as per the clinic's standing protocol or a doctor's order
- Practice: BLS on a manikin with a certified instructor; two timed mock emergencies

lessons.title: Counselling and teach-back
lessons.description: The nurse explains procedures and aftercare clearly and confirms understanding.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Explaining the procedure, what to expect, warning signs, aftercare, follow-up
- Teach-back to confirm understanding
- Practice: counsel 5 mock patients

lessons.title: Supervised practice, logbook and exams
lessons.description: 8 hours supervised practice, then the knowledge test, two practical exams and the emergency drill.
lessons.transcript:
Assessment: knowledge test 50 MCQ in 75 minutes (pass 80%); practical exam 1 (instrument reprocessing and tray set-up); practical exam 2 (pre-procedure checklist, assisting a mock procedure, counselling); emergency drill (BLS on manikin and mock anaphylaxis, 100% of critical steps).
Logbook minimums before Level 1: instrument reprocessing cycles 20; procedures assisted 30; charts completed and checked 40; medication checks with a senior nurse 30; emergency drills 2.

questions.q: Recommended adult chest-compression rate in BLS is:
questions.e: Adult BLS uses 100–120 compressions per minute.

questions.q: Adult compression depth should be about:
questions.e: Compress about 5–6 cm with full recoil.

questions.q: Before administering any medication you must confirm:
o: Right patient, drug, dose, route and time
That a colleague used it yesterday
questions.e: The medication 'rights' are verified every time.

questions.q: A sterilised pack has a chemical indicator that did not change colour. You:
o: Treat the pack as non-sterile and reprocess it
questions.e: An indicator failure means sterility is not assured. Do not use and reprocess.

checklist.title: Staff Nurse practical stations
checklist.description: Sterilisation, emergency drill, procedure assistance and logbook.

items.label: Logbook completed and signed by trainer

courses.title: Housekeeping Training
courses.short_description: A 6-day, 36-hour programme teaching the exact cleaning routines, chemical safety and waste handling used in every VTIARA branch.
courses.overview: Housekeeping staff keep treatment rooms safe and clean; one missed step can spread infection. The 6 days (16 hours of Common Core plus 20 hours of housekeeping) are taught mostly through pictures and demonstrations, in Kannada, Hindi or the local language, with English terms for chemicals and equipment. You may never touch used sharps, handle lasers or other devices, move patient records, or enter a procedure room during a procedure without a nurse or doctor present.
courses.audience: Housekeeping and support staff, new hires and existing staff.
eligibility: 8th to 10th pass; can read labels and simple instructions
Hepatitis B vaccination recommended before joining
outcomes: Clean and reset treatment rooms, waiting areas, washrooms and corridors
Mix and use approved disinfectants as taught
Segregate and move biomedical waste to the storage area
Handle linen and towels safely
Clean small spills using the spill kit
requirements_text: 100% attendance
80% or higher on the knowledge test
All practical checklist items passed
Yearly refresher

lessons.title: Clean first, then disinfect
lessons.description: Staff can pick the right cloth, mop and product and handle chemicals safely.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Clean first, then disinfect: dirt blocks disinfectants
- Colour-coded cloths and mops: red for toilets and washroom floors, yellow for washbasins and taps, blue for treatment rooms and reception, green for pantry

lessons.title: Chemical safety
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Read the label every time; wear gloves and, where the label says so, eye protection
- Never mix chemicals; bleach mixed with acids or ammonia products gives toxic gas
- Keep every bottle labelled; never pour chemicals into drink bottles
- Practice: identify 10 products from labels; match product to area

modules.title: H2 Disinfectants, room routines and spills

lessons.title: Dilution and contact time
lessons.description: Staff can dilute correctly, clean a room in the right order and manage a spill.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Dilution and contact time come from the product label; typical chlorine strengths 0.1% (1,000 ppm) for general surfaces and 1% (10,000 ppm) for blood or body-fluid spills; confirm with the branch policy
- Make fresh solution each day and label it with date and time

lessons.title: Cleaning order and high-touch surfaces
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Clean to dirty, top to bottom, far to near; use two-bucket mopping
- High-touch surfaces first: door handles, switches, bed rails, trolley handles, chair arms, taps

lessons.title: Room turnover and spills
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Treatment room turnover between patients, end-of-day deep clean, washroom routine
- Spill response (SOP-HK-04)
- Practice: dilution exercise with measuring cups; timed cleaning of a mock treatment room (target 10 minutes)

modules.title: H3 Biomedical waste, linen, procedure and laser rooms

lessons.title: Biomedical waste colour bins
lessons.description: Staff separate waste correctly, handle linen safely and respect procedure and laser room rules.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Yellow: soiled dressings, cotton, gauze, contaminated items, expired medicines; red: contaminated plastics such as tubing, syringes without needles, gloves
- White translucent puncture-proof container: needles and blades; blue box: glass vials and ampoules; black bag: general waste
- Confirm current Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 and your waste vendor's instructions

lessons.title: Handling and storing waste
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Never mix categories; fill bags only up to three-quarters; never press down a bag; never put hands inside; label with date and branch
- Keep a waste register; store in the locked waste room; hand over only to the authorised vendor

lessons.title: Linen, procedure rooms and laser rooms
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Linen: wear gloves, do not shake, carry in a closed bag, keep soiled linen apart
- Laser room: enter only when the nurse says the device is off; never touch a device or move cables
- Never touch a loose needle or blade: stay away and call the nurse
- Practice: sort 30 items into bins; visit the waste room and read the register

lessons.title: Supervised practice and sign-off
lessons.description: 4 hours cleaning real rooms with a buddy using the checklists, then 2 hours knowledge test and practical check.
lessons.transcript: Pass rule: 100% attendance, 80% on the knowledge test, all practical checklist items passed. Certificate: Hygiene Certificate, valid 12 months, then yearly refresher.

questions.q: Which must you never mix?
questions.e: Mixing bleach with ammonia or acids can release toxic gas.

questions.q: You find a blood spill. First you:
o: Wipe it with a dry cloth
Wear PPE, contain and treat the spill per protocol
Cover it with a towel and leave
Ask a patient to avoid it
questions.e: Wear PPE, contain and disinfect using the clinic's spill procedure.

questions.q: When cleaning a treatment room you work:
o: Clean to dirty, top to bottom
questions.e: Clean-to-dirty and top-to-bottom avoids spreading contamination.

questions.q: In a laser room with the 'laser in use' sign lit, you:
o: Do not enter until the treatment ends and it is declared safe
questions.e: Never enter while the laser is in use; follow the room's safety instructions.

items.label: Wears correct PPE and performs hand hygiene
Uses correct disinfectant dilution and contact time

courses.title: Telecaller Training
courses.short_description: A 2-week, 74-hour programme building listening, accurate information, clean data entry and legal compliance for the first voice of VTIARA.
courses.overview: The telecaller is the first voice of VTIARA; one honest, warm call turns an enquiry into a safe first visit. Over 2 weeks (16 hours of Common Core plus 58 telecaller hours), then 3 days of monitored live calls, you learn patient communication and voice, treatment knowledge, six call flows, CRM use, ethical objection handling, compliance and scored mock calls.
courses.audience: New telecallers who handle enquiries, appointment booking, follow-up and reminders.
eligibility: Clear spoken English plus the local language of the market
outcomes: Sound warm, clear and calm, and listen before speaking
Explain each treatment in simple, approved words and know what not to say
Follow the six call flows from opening to close
Record every call outcome accurately in the CRM the same day
Handle objections honestly without pressure
Follow consent, DND and telecom commercial-communication rules
requirements_text: 80% or higher on the knowledge test
Mock-call average of 85% with no critical error
3 days of monitored live calls reviewed

lessons.title: Voice
lessons.description: The telecaller sounds warm, clear and calm, and listens before speaking.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Voice: pace, tone, smile in the voice, pausing, avoiding fillers and slang

lessons.title: Listening and language
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Let the patient finish, repeat back the concern, ask one question at a time
- Simple words in English and the local language; no medical jargon; spell out names and numbers

lessons.title: Anxious, angry or confused patients
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Stay calm, apologise for the inconvenience, fix the problem or escalate
- Practice: recorded 1-minute calls, playback and feedback

lessons.title: Explaining common treatments
lessons.description: The telecaller can explain each treatment in simple, approved words and knows what not to say.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- For each common treatment (acne care, pigmentation, hair fall treatments, PRP and mesotherapy, laser hair reduction, anti-ageing facials and peels, dandruff care): what it is, who it may suit, typical sessions, visit time, general downtime

lessons.title: What to always add
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- The doctor decides after examination; results vary; no guarantees
- Prices and packages: where to find the current approved list

lessons.title: Questions to transfer
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Transfer to the nurse or doctor: pregnancy, medicines, reactions, pain, anything about a current treatment
- Practice: explain 5 treatments in 30 seconds each; quiz with a nurse

lessons.title: The six call flows
lessons.description: The telecaller follows the six VTIARA call flows with a clear opening, discovery, next step and close.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- New enquiry, appointment booking, reminder, reschedule and cancellation, follow-up after visit, complaint call

lessons.title: Structure of every call
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Opening, discovery questions, summary, next step and polite closing
- Practice: 15 scripted calls, then unscripted

lessons.title: Leads, fields and disposition codes
lessons.description: The telecaller records every call accurately in the CRM the same day.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Create and update a lead; required fields; disposition codes; follow-up dates; notes in plain facts

lessons.title: Same-day updates and data privacy
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Same-day update rule; duplicate checking; no patient data in personal notes or chats
- Practice: 20 entries in the practice CRM; error review

modules.title: T5 Objection handling and ethical selling

lessons.title: Listen, acknowledge, answer, offer
lessons.description: The telecaller answers concerns with facts and offers a consultation, never pressure.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Listen, acknowledge, answer with facts, offer the next step (a consultation), never pressure

lessons.title: Common objections
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Price, fear, time, 'I will think', 'another clinic is cheaper', 'is it safe?'
- Never create false urgency or exaggerated claims
- Practice: role-play 10 objections with a coach

lessons.title: Who you may call
lessons.description: The telecaller follows consent, telecom and privacy rules on every call.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Call only people who enquired or consented; honour do-not-disturb requests and the telecom commercial-communication rules (DND registry, registered sender and templates) as confirmed by the legal advisor

lessons.title: Recording, privacy and claims
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- Tell patients when calls are recorded; never share patient details with anyone else
- No claims of guaranteed results, cure, or medical advice; no fake urgency
- Practice: spot the violations in 8 sample calls

lessons.title: Mock calls with coach feedback
lessons.description: The telecaller reaches an 85% average on scored mock calls with no critical error.
lessons.transcript:
Key points:
- 20 mock calls scored with the call scoring sheet; coach feedback after each 5

modules.title: Knowledge test, call exam and monitored live calls

lessons.title: Knowledge test, call exam and monitored live calls
lessons.description: 2 hours knowledge test and call exam, followed by 3 days of monitored live calls with a buddy.
lessons.transcript:
Pass rule: 80% on the knowledge test; mock-call average 85% with no critical error; 3 days of live calls reviewed. Certificate: Telecaller Level 1, valid 12 months.
Rules of the role: never diagnose, advise on medicines or promise results; quote only approved prices, packages and offers; call only people who have enquired or given consent; tell the patient when a call is recorded; record every call outcome in the CRM the same day.

questions.q: A number is on the DND registry and the person has not asked to be called. For a promotional call you:
o: Send a promotional SMS from a personal number
questions.e: Promotional calls to numbers on the DND registry are not allowed without valid consent.

questions.q: A caller asks whether a treatment will 'definitely' cure their problem. You:
o: Promise a cure to book the appointment
Avoid guarantees and invite them for a doctor consultation
questions.e: Never guarantee outcomes. Invite the patient for a consultation.

questions.q: A caller asks you to diagnose their rash. You:
o: Explain you cannot diagnose and offer a doctor consultation
questions.e: Telecallers never diagnose or prescribe.

questions.q: A person claiming to be a relative asks for a patient's appointment details. You:
o: Do not share without authorised verification
questions.e: Patient information is confidential and shared only after proper verification.

checklist.title: Mock calls and monitored live calls
checklist.description: Mock-call score (minimum 85%), compliance check and monitored live-call approval.

items.label: Compliance script check (DND, consent, no guarantees)
